content: 1. Do not encourage the woman to push unless instructed by a healthcare professional. Pushing prematurely can lead to complications. 2. Follow only the advice provided by the healthcare worker and avoid giving additional or conflicting instructions. 3. During the first stage of labor, when the cervix is dilated 0-3 cm and contractions are weak and infrequent (less than 2 in 10 minutes), monitor the woman every hour for emergency signs using rapid assessment. 4. Assess the frequency, intensity, and duration of contractions, fetal heart rate, and cervical dilation. Vaginal examinations should not be performed more frequently than every 4 hours unless clinically indicated. 5. Regularly monitor the woman’s temperature, pulse, and blood pressure, and record findings in the labor record and partograph. 6. Document the time of membrane rupture and the color of the amniotic fluid. 7. Provide supportive care and ensure the woman is never left alone. If complications arise, refer the woman urgently to a hospital. 8. Discharge the woman only if her condition is stable and advise her to return if pain or discomfort increases, vaginal bleeding occurs, or membranes rupture. 9. During active labor (cervix dilated 4 cm or more), monitor every 30 minutes for emergency signs, contractions, fetal heart rate, and cervical dilation. 10. Encourage the woman to empty her bladder and maintain adequate hydration, but avoid solid foods. 11. Support the woman in an upright position or walking if she wishes, and monitor her progress intensively. 12. If labor does not progress after 2 hours, reassess and refer to a hospital if necessary. Do not wait for the action line to be crossed if referral takes time. 13. In the second stage of labor (cervix fully dilated, perineum bulging, and head visible), monitor every 5 minutes for emergency signs, contractions, fetal heart rate, and visible descent of the fetal head. 14. Ensure all delivery equipment, including newborn resuscitation supplies, is available, and the delivery area is clean and warm (25°C). 15. Assist the woman into a comfortable, upright position of her choice and provide emotional and physical support. 16. Do not allow the woman to lie flat on her back. If she is distressed, encourage pain relief techniques. 17. Allow the woman to push as she wishes with contractions but do not urge her to push. 18. If the perineum does not thin and stretch after 30 minutes of spontaneous pushing, perform a vaginal examination to confirm full cervical dilation. If not fully dilated, discourage pushing and encourage breathing techniques. 19. During delivery, ensure controlled delivery of the baby’s head by gently supporting it as it advances with contractions. Support the perineum with one hand and cover the anus with a pad. 20. Check for the umbilical cord around the baby’s neck. If loose, slip it over the baby’s head; if tight, clamp and cut the cord before unwinding it. 21. Wipe the baby’s face clean if necessary, but routine suctioning is not recommended unless dense substances block the nose or mouth. 22. Allow spontaneous rotation of the shoulders and delivery within 1-2 minutes. Apply gentle downward pressure to deliver the top shoulder, then lift the baby upward to deliver the lower shoulder. 23. Place the baby on the mother’s abdomen or in her arms for skin-to-skin contact. If this is not possible, place the baby in a clean, warm, safe area close to the mother. 24. Thoroughly dry the baby immediately, wipe the eyes, and discard the wet cloth. Assess the baby’s breathing while drying. 25. If the baby is not crying, observe for effective breathing (chest rising). If not breathing or gasping, stimulate by rubbing the back 2-3 times and start newborn resuscitation if necessary. 26. Clamp and cut the umbilical cord 1-3 minutes after birth, ensuring ties are secure. Do not bandage or bind the stump. 27. Encourage breastfeeding within the first hour after birth. If the mother is HIV-infected and has chosen replacement feeding, follow her feeding plan. 28. In the third stage of labor (delivery of the placenta), monitor the mother every 5 minutes and the baby every 15 minutes for emergency signs. 29. Ensure the uterus is well-contracted and there is no heavy bleeding. If bleeding persists, massage the uterus to expel clots and administer oxytocin. 30. Deliver the placenta using controlled cord traction while applying counter-traction to the uterus. If the placenta does not descend within 30-40 seconds, release traction and wait for the uterus to contract again before repeating. 31. If the placenta is not delivered within 30 minutes of oxytocin administration and the woman is not bleeding, encourage breastfeeding and repeat controlled cord traction. If bleeding occurs, manage as per protocol. 32. If the placenta is not delivered within 1 hour, remove it manually or refer the woman to a hospital urgently. 33. Check that the placenta and membranes are complete. If incomplete, remove placental fragments manually. 34. If heavy bleeding persists despite uterine massage and oxytocin, apply bimanual or aortic compression and refer the woman urgently to a hospital. 35. For third-degree tears involving the rectum or anus, refer urgently to a hospital. For other tears, apply pressure with a sterile pad and repair if bleeding persists. 36. Estimate and record blood loss throughout the third stage and afterward. If blood loss is approximately 250 mL but bleeding has stopped, monitor the woman intensively for 4 hours and assist her when she first walks. 37. Clean the woman and the area beneath her, and help her change clothes if necessary. Keep the mother and baby in the delivery room for at least 1 hour after placenta delivery. 38. Dispose of the placenta safely and appropriately, using gloves and a leak-proof container. 39. If fetal heart rate (FHR) is <120 or >160 beats per minute, position the woman on her left side and check for a prolapsed cord or meconium-stained liquor. Repeat FHR count after 15 minutes. 40. If the cord is prolapsed, manage urgently by elevating the presenting part and referring the woman to a hospital. Expedite delivery if in late labor. 41. If the baby is not well, prepare for newborn resuscitation and explain the situation to the mother and her companion. 42. For breech presentation, confirm full cervical dilation and ensure the bladder is empty. Assist the woman into a position that allows the baby to hang down during delivery. Prepare for newborn resuscitation and expedite delivery if necessary.
